newsitem.title: POLAND: Budapest leads E.Europe bourses after rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Budapest leads E.Europe bourses after rate rise.

text.p: The Budapest bourse received a boost this week once it put the U.S. Federal Reserve's Funds rate rise behind it, but analysts in Warsaw and Prague saw no reason for joy in coming days apart from the Easter holiday.
Romanian shares gained this week but Slovenia, Croatia and Slovakia all saw losses.
The Central European Share Index (CESI) of 73 selected Czech, Polish, Hungarian, Slovak and Slovenian stocks rose 2.7 percent on the week to 1,545.77 points.
BUDAPEST

Investors' scaled-down activity kept market volume and price movements low in the first two days of the week but the Fed's 25-basis-point rate hike on Tuesday swept away fears, giving room for massive rises on Wednesday and Thursday.
On Thursday the BUX index finished at 5,438.97 points, up 354.17 from last Friday, gaining almost three percent both on Thursday and Friday.

"Investors' appetite grew, it seems this still stems from the rate hike," said Laszlo Baranyai of Gog Securities. "The other factor is that new market players entered the market, bringing fresh funds."
Quiet trade is seen for Friday.
WARSAW
Polish shares are seen falling next week after this week's 4.5 percent gain, as analysts said the market, with a current price-earnings ratio of 15.6, looked fairly valued at best.
They said the bourse, currently at 16,690.4 points, could fall toward 16,000 points next week or stabilise.
Analysts were cheered that the market had survived the U.S.'s 25-basis-point Funds rate rise on Tuesday but said this did not necessarily provide a platform for growth.
"The fact the rise has been discounted does not mean that a long period of growth awaits us," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
The bourse is closed on Friday and Monday.
PRAGUE
Czech shares ended their downtrend on the Prague Stock Exchange this week with a mid-week blue chip rally, though traders said the halt may be only temporary.
The PX50 index edged up 0.6 points to 558.3 as major issues SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka all broke out of their slump on Wednesday.
But dealers said they saw no real change in market sentiment, with a lack of foreign players keeping volumes low.
"In the short-term, the strengthening will not continue, there's absolutely no reason why the market should change its downward trend," said Radek Vavra of Citicorp Securities in Prague.
Dealers said poorer-than-expected macroeconomic data in recent weeks, coupled with disappointing company results, have also helped dampen investor interest.
BRATISLAVA

The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) saw another week of low trading activity, caused mainly by a lack of interest among foreign investors, but traders said this might change soon as the market's blue chips now looked cheap.
The official 16-share SAX index eased 1.62 points to 207.02 on Thursday from its year-high of 208.64 last Friday.
Dealers noted that foreign investors, who are the only players to give the market impetus for longer-term trends, may soon return to pick up some undervalued shares.
"They can come out of the blue, as, for example, VSZ or Slovnaft appear to be the region's cheapest shares in their field," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares fell 3.29 percent this week as the blue-chip SBI index was down 43.55 points to 1,277.69. Turnover was at 272.5 million tolars ($1.8 million).
Bank SKB was the leading decliner, down 9.8 percent, while warehouse and shopping center operator BTC was the top gainer, up 4.8 percent.
The Ljubljana bourse is closed for Easter on Monday.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks extended their losses on Thursday after trading lower throughout the week while blue chips held their ground.
Analysts saw few price changes in the next two weeks.
Apart from the usual pre-Easter lull they said investors were also holding back until the financial results of fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva are released next month.
BUCHAREST
Activity was buoyant on the Bucharest bourse this week with turnover rising to over eight billion lei in three trading sessions from last week's six billion.
Investors focused again on first-tier heavyweights Oltchim SA chemical plant and Azomures SA fertiliser maker, while small-cap trading recovered on Thursday after a dull period earlier in the week.
